newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian courier firm plans Bergamo Fokker flights.
newsitem.headline: Belgian courier firm plans Bergamo Fokker flights.

text.p: TBC Halbart Aviation, a Belgian privately-owned courier company, plans to start a Fokker 27 service between Brussels and Bergamo, director Claude Rombaux told Reuters.
The six-tonne capacity Fokker replaces a Metro III on the route, which has a capacity of two tonnes. The five-strong-fleet airline began its Bergamo service in January last year.
Bergamo is the company's sub-hub serving destinations such as Verona, Milan, Florence and Rome. In the future the courier company will also truck cargo to Switzerland from Bergamo.
TBC Halbart Aviation was set up in May 1995 to offer an alternative to the express product of DHL Worldwide Express in Brussels, said Rombaux.
It aims to create a total European network and will move towards using larger six tonne aircraft.
The company handles courier business for Airborne Express, Skynet and Jet Services amongst others.
It also operates services to Madrid, Barcelona, London and Copenhagen with a Fokker 27, Metro III aircraft and Short 360s, which have a capacity of 3.6 tonnes.
Rombaux said there are plans to start a service between Madrid, Lisbon and Brussels at end-March.
Also the company plans to operate larger aircraft on the Madrid, Barcelona and Copenhagen routes. Bergamo-Rome is also under consideration, he added.
TBC also plans to open its own office in Paris by the end of April and an office in Bergamo is being established.
Rombaux said its express business is increasing rather than general airfreight.
"TBC Halbart Aviation initially employed two people in 1995 but it now employs 36 people, has seven trucks and five aircraft", said Rombaux. --Reuters Air Cargo News Tel+44-171-542-7706b Fax 5017
